newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks reverse early advance to end down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks reverse early advance to end down.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed early gains at the close Friday on profit-taking triggered when the Dow Jones industrial average pared an initial advance.
They added that dealing was slowed down by the holiday season.
"Some sellers stepped in, who were on the sidelines yesterday; dealers took profits and the Dow turnaround hit us a little," a dealer said.

The blue chip IPC index ended off 18.78 points, or 0.56 percent, at 3,311.36. Volume was 177.2 million shares traded, 91 million of which were accounted for by mining firm Camesa, which ended off 1 centavo (1 cent) at 3.46 pesos (44 cents).
"The session was somewhat dull. Volume was not bad, but most of it was due to cross trades. Almost every one was just waiting for the bell, to go out and party," a trader said.
A total of 103 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered gainers by 50 to 32.
Traders noted the presence of market heavyweight Telmex among the sliders, off 12 centavos (2 cents) at 12.48 pesos ($1.59), while its ADRs fell 37.5 cents in New York to $31.75.
Another notable loser, traders said, was media group Televisa, off 3 pesos (38 cents) at 101 pesos ($12.87) in Mexico, while its ADRs slid 25 cents to $26.
Blue chips were conspicuously absent from the gainers list, with cement firm Cemex a notable exception, traders said. Cemex closed up 10 centavos (1 cent) at 28.35 pesos ($3.61).
Debt-stricken Grupo Sidek headed the leaders, up 17 centavos (2 cents) at 90 centavos (11 cents), but at light trade and on technicals, traders said.
Technical analysts said the bourse was still in a consolidation period.

"We're just gathering a head of steam before continuing on the upside. We're consolidating to pave the way for higher levels by year's end, but do not expect any surprises," said one technical analyst.
